data.title: Inadequate Protection of Server and Comms Rooms
data.summary: Server and communications rooms were protected only by the same credential that opens general office doors, were left unlocked, or were reachable through shared spaces, allowing physical access to equipment that bypasses most logical controls.
data.description:
Physical access to infrastructure is equivalent to administrative access, and in some respects exceeds it. At the rack an attacker can connect to management ports and console interfaces, boot a server from external media, remove or image a disk, attach a device to a switch or tap a fibre, and in many environments reach backup media stored in the same room.

Comms cupboards on each floor are often overlooked while the main server room is well controlled, yet they offer the same switch access and are protected by a standard key that many people hold.

Shared buildings add routes that the tenant does not control: suspended ceilings and raised floors spanning partition walls, and landlord maintenance access out of hours.
data.recommendation:
* Control technical rooms with credentials distinct from general office access, granted to a short named list and reviewed quarterly.
* Log and monitor every entry, and alert on access outside maintenance windows.
* Lock racks themselves, so room access does not grant equipment access.
* Address ceiling and floor void bypasses with physical barriers, and verify them rather than assuming.
* Disable or restrict console and out-of-band management ports that are not in use.
data.short_recommendation: Separately control, log and monitor access to technical rooms.
